utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is the case number IT-97-25-T, the Prosecutor versus Milorad Krnojelac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: What is AID, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: AID is part of the police forces in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And it assisted the Tribunal in such way that the Tribunal staff, of course, did not know where all the localities were where the witnesses were living, so we always informed the AID which witness we wanted to interview and then this witness was brought in and was interviewed and brought back, and police officers from this office did this transport and informed the witnesses that they wanted to be interviewed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And kept some note of their address --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: -- in case they had to be contacted.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Especially the witnesses in Sarajevo, when they were in Sarajevo, either lived in refugee places or switched living quarters quite often because they didn't have homes - they came from Foca - and therefore we never knew where they were living.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just as a matter of interest, what does AID, the acronym, stand for?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I'm not absolutely sure, but what I know is that it is an English abbreviation. It's Agency for Information -- but there's something in between. But we will have a witness who can explain that to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. If I may say, I also tried to find out something about it. My learned friend is right; it is a part of the police force, but as far as I know, that is the state security, a kind of a secret service. But that is the information that I received about AID, if this is any help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It does not sound very sinister, if I may say so. Anyway, you proceed with your cross-examination. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Bakrac: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you ready? Can you answer some more questions in cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday you showed us where your room was at the time of the incident with Mr. Zekovic. I shall now move on to specific incidents which you described, or rather that you testified during your examination-in-chief. In direct examination you said that after beatings and screams, you heard shots, and after that a splash of water; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, in your statement which you gave to the OTP in 1995, you said the following -- I apologise. It is the first statement, 1995, page 6, the first passage: "Those who were called out did not return, as a rule. I think they were killed. My assumption is corroborated by the fact that the prisoners of the upper floor could hear sounds of something splashing, falling into the water, at night." So my question is: Which of the two statements is correct? Did you hear those splashes or is it that these sounds could be heard by prisoners on upper floors?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I listened to what you said. In one sentence you say one thing and in the second sentence you say a different thing. But these two things are related, which means - and I want to say on this occasion - the building that we were in was elevated above the offices so that tortures and rapes could be heard more clearly in the upper part of the building and worse in the lower part of the building, but they could be heard in both of them, and at that time you could hear a needle fall in the compound because those tortures lay in store for every inmate. After this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Stop, sir, just stop. Let us start today by trying to answer the question. The question was related to hearing splashing in the water. You haven't even got near to that now. The question is: Did you hear the splashing in the water or are you relying solely upon what you were told by the people upstairs? Now, that's the question you were asked and we would like an answer.

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tortures and splashes, we both heard them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you tell the OTP, then, that it was heard by prisoners on the upper floors and not you yourself?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I say before the court again that the splash had so many decibels, then those above could hear those splashes against the water much louder than we did. That is my explanation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, in your -- during the direct examination, you said, "We heard splashes against the water. You can invite an expert, an expert witness, to check that." Nobody challenged that. Why did you say that? Nobody disputed that when you raised that matter.

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am responsible for the answers that I give, and I always say, if somebody does not believe any of those things that I said, can go to the scene, which is now accessible, and check it on the spot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But why did you, about this specific thing, suggest that it be checked even though nobody had challenged before that? Did you follow the trial before you came here?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not follow any of the trials.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you talk before your testimony with somebody about this case?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the testimony, I discussed -- I did discuss this trial but what I said, I stand by it, and that is why I say all the words that I utter before this Honourable Court, please check them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who did you talk with about it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I might make confessions to you and tell you who are all the people that I talked to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do I understand you, you refuse to tell us who you discussed it with?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said at the beginning of the trial that to my mind, the lawyer is asking me questions which are very provocative and expects me to answer them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sir, you are being asked who you spoke to about it. It's a perfectly permissible question. If you don't want to tell us, you say so and then we will worry about the consequences if that is the case. But it's not for you to determine what is relevant and what is not relevant. Now, are you prepared to identify who you spoke to about this before the trial -- before you gave evidence?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. President, I am not familiar with legal laws and therefore I cannot answer that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The question was very simple. Are you prepared to tell us who you spoke to? Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour maybe the witness spoke with other protected witnesses and maybe it's easier for him to write down the names, if it is so. I don't know. It may be. It may be that this is a problem, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Well, if you have some worry about the identity of the person you spoke to becoming public, you may write it down but we will not look at it unless the Defence counsel is also allowed to look at it. Now, are you prepared to identify who you spoke to?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can write down the names of people I talked to with these conversations that I had. I don't know what they mean to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: As I say, that's not a matter for you. If you will write them down now and then they will be shown to counsel.

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [witness writes]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, you could check that for any protected witnesses, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: These are not protected witnesses.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Sorry. These are not protected witnesses. These are witnesses but they will come here and testify openly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Bakrac, my intention at the moment is to simply mark that as an exhibit under seal. Whilst the witnesses are not protected, this witness may feel some diffidence about them knowing that he has revealed that fact, so that we will be able to refer to them. If you need to refer to them, you may do so by reference to the document but -- and the document will be under seal. Have you any objection to that procedure?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. That's quite acceptable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That document will be Exhibit P433 and it is under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, may I proceed?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from the individuals whose name you have written down, sir, did you talk with somebody else before you came to give your testimony?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the place that I -- in the place that I come from, I didn't discuss this with anyone there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And outside the place that you've come from?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Outside the place that I've come from, I've already written the names of people that I talked with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And nobody else?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember that there was anybody else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, I asked you, and I am asking you again now, when we've -- when we read what you had said in your first statement and what you had said in the direct examination, did you hear shots and splashes against the water?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you mention the shots before?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll tell the Defence. After this ill-famed camp, my head reels, and it would take a month of complete rest to describe every detail before this court. Because things that went on were such that one thinks, well, if I say I heard a -- this, am I to now explain how many decibels was the sound of a pistol, how many decibels were screams? But what I am saying is that I heard it, and both the upper and the lower floors heard it, those on the upper floor with more decibels and those on the lower floors with less decibels. That is my statement, if you get my meaning, and this is the third time I repeat this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Because just now you told us that there were so many crimes committed there, I will read to you something that you told the OTP: "I never witnessed a crime because I was locked up in my cell."

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true - you, Defence - that during that 12 days that I was in the cell, I did not hear it, because I was so badly beaten that I couldn't hear the movements of my body. That is correct about those 12 days. But two years and six months, where are they?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never mentioned any 12 days.

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I kept mentioning 12 days after the beating. That was in the camp, when the person concerned fled the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke in general. That is not the part where you referred to Zekovic. You simply say that you did not eyewitness the crimes.

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand you. You are saying one thing about those 12 days; now you are saying something else which has nothing to do with those 12 days. And I repeat again: I spent two years and six months in the camp, and 12 days I spent in a cell, and there I could not even hear the movements of my body, let alone something else, during those 12 days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were locked all 12 days and you could not move about?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent all those 12 days in the isolation cell. I couldn't make a single move. Now, for the first time that day, when he was found that day, I was forced out into the yard to see the man who had been captured, and you've got to go out when you're ordered, even if all the bones in your body are broken. There's no --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said, "because I was locked in my cell." You never mentioned the isolation cell or 12 days. It is in that part where you spoke about what had been going on in the KP Dom in general.

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat: My cell, that cell of mine. I would have stayed in that cell of mine to this day, when you say "my cell."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does it mean, "stay to this day"? Are you trying to be ironic? I never thought to say that the cell was your property.

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Will you please ask me the question that you want an answer to in two or three words, not a sentence? One is like this, and then after that comes another sentence with a different meaning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I've heard enough about this. Did you ever mention a court martial?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of us who were in the camp knew that there was a court martial outside in Foca, and it was in operation at that time in Foca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you learn about that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything that went on in the compound and outside the compound, we knew about it all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How could you know about this court martial?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the murder of Isanovic, Selimovic, and the surname of the third person whom I don't know, who I guess was not born in the town, Serb guards, that is, one of the Serb guards, told us the court martial -- those three individuals were court martialled, that they are three persons whom the extremist part of the SDS had condemned without any defence or anything, and they allegedly sentenced those three persons to be immediately taken before the firing squad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was very simple: Where and how did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We heard it in the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From whom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I point out before the Honourable Court that the lawyer seeks names of honest Serbs, and in that part -- and there are still extremists there, so that I should like to ask the Honourable Court to say I should not even write those names for him, because I know what will happen to those honest people. If I may ask that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, this is the point that the witness took yesterday afternoon -- I'm sorry, yesterday morning. It's a view which is one which he very strongly holds, obviously. Whether it's justified or not is not really a matter for us. I think we all recognise that a failure or a refusal to identify such persons must have some bearing on the weight to be afforded to his evidence, but I would not myself like to force him to do so. He made it very clear that he believes that you or those around you will reveal them to people who will then cause trouble for the persons he names. As I say, we're not going to buy into that. But his refusal, for whatever reason, to identify them clearly does have some effect on the weight of the evidence he's given. I think that probably is sufficient for your purposes, unless you wish to pursue the matter further.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I fully agree. I do not want to insist on this really. I'll ask only one question about this, and I'm not asking for any names. And I'll try to finish this witness as Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. quickly as possible, and I do believe that it will come to an end shortly. I know; I also would be very happy if the answers were shorter and more precise, but what can I do?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you remember saying to the OTP that you learnt about the court martial on the radio?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not quite sure, but it is possible that I said that, because those were the early days. It was in the early days of the war, so that we also had a radio. But even without the radio, we learned this information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you spoke, sir, about persons -- or rather, that other prisoners had heard something splashing against the water, you also then stated that on the radio you heard later on that the bodies of those prisoners had been found in Gorazde; is that true?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which radio station?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I shall be shorter today. Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which radio station? Will you wait for my question to be interpreted.

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat once again what I repeated yesterday and the day before yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you would not be repeating yourself, you would give us short answers. My question was: Which radio did you hear it on?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radio Sarajevo, report from Foca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from Foca they reported that the bodies of those prisoners had been found in Gorazde, which was then under Muslim control?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. I'm referring to bodies which were thrown from the bridge, and those other bodies which were killed in the hospital, they stayed there and the mother sent the godfather of this young man to Foca from Cajnice so that --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's not beat about the bush here. I'm referring to bodies which were thrown from the bridge. You told us that you heard on the radio that they had been found in Gorazde. Are you telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was a report from Foca for Radio Sarajevo, is it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that a woman from Serb origin told the journalist Semso Tucakovic, who then broadcast it on the radio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that woman of Serb origin, was she in Foca?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was in Foca. She was killed -- she was found dead, and after that we could not hear anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But how could she know what had been found in Gorazde if there was a front line between Foca and Gorazde?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we are in the middle ages and the telephones do not exist. It is very difficult to cover those 30 kilometres with the radio stations. Radio station and transistors and receivers do not exist, you mean we are still in the middle ages. Is that what you're saying? So there was no way she could find that out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir, very much. I shall move on specifically to names that you gave us here. I will ask you about Professor Dzelilovic. You mentioned him. Was his father in the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when he was taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I -- dates, I -- well, he was there for a short while and then he disappeared and was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us which room he was taken from?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was separated from those collective rooms -- four of us who worked distributing food, we were separated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that you do not know what room he was taken from, is it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that room was on the first floor because I know from the kitchen one could see who comes from which floor, first floor, and I really didn't care about room, whether this room or that room. I don't even know which room I was in because I was in all of them, so that I didn't care about the numbers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see who took him out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat before the Honourable Court - and this is the hundredth time I repeat this - the order from the administration, arrival of officers as we had to call them, taking out and disappearance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is specific: Which officer took him out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer that because I couldn't even watch it anymore, there were so many of these, so many were taken out. And it never crossed my mind to try to remember which officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time of the day was it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think -- well, as a rule they took people out in late afternoon. That is when it usually happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At about what time in late afternoon?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it depends on the season of the year, and that was spring time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if the summer, then it's 8.00 or 9.00?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was spring time, so it could have been around 4.00 or 5.00, half past five, 6.00, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you when he was taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the canteen. It was before the dinner or perhaps it was the end of it, so that -- I spent the whole day in the restaurant while I worked in the restaurant, that is, in the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But were you working or watching through the window?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me explain. When we finish our work, then we have to make the fire beneath the caldron, so that we are in the yard. The caldron was outside because -- because we used firewood to cook meals, if that means anything to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was food prepared in this one caldron for everybody in the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For all the inmates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the Serb prisoners and others who ate there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It changed later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether there was a separate caldron.

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At first, at first, it was the same. And later, we were replaced. Serbs came to work at this caldron. At first, it was -- when we were first detained, there was one caldron, and then later on we were replaced by Serbs, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they cooked using this same caldron?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They cooked using the same caldron, I think, because they had there even greater extremists, the way they looked at it, so they were also beaten, yes, battered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned a person with the last name of Vahida. Do you know when he was taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vahida also during these first months was beaten, battered and taken out. I saw him a few days, for a few days, when he was beaten up and when he came to eat. After that he was taken out, killed, and he went missing. It was that group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether you saw when he was taken out.

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every inmate --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please answer me specifically. Did you see him? I'm not asking you about what other inmates saw.

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember this moment. I mean to tell you the exact time, whatever. I mean, I'd have to have a computer rather than a head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just asking you whether you saw him.

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At first, I saw everybody who was taken out and remembered him too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether you saw him being taken out and when he went missing or, as you say, when he was killed.

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I told you I remembered everybody I knew because there would be commotion immediately at any time during the night. Even the Serbs who would stay there would say, "They are taking out these guys," and even when there were only four of us in this room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, let's make it easier for the court and for everyone. There are quite a few names. I would like to move from one name to another and I'd like to ask you about the details, the time and the place where these persons were taken from so that we would not waste time. Just tell me, please, whether you can say for all of these persons, whether they were taken out, when they were taken out, where they were taken out, by who they were taken out, and where you were? Or can you simply not tell us any of this?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can. I can say, but who took them out, it didn't mean a thing to me or to the other inmates. These younger men remembered all the names of these people who took them out and we know through who they got orders to take them out. I mean, if this is clear to you, if my answer is clear to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think the answer is clear enough that he cannot tell us who took them out. And I think he's also said he can't say the time. Now, if there are any other details, you take him to those.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I also asked whether he knew in which rooms these persons were. Of course, I agree with what you've said specifically. And also, where was he? Did he see everybody individually as they were taken out and then never returned?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Those are the details I suggest that you ask him specifically in relation to the particular matters, and we will see how we go.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned a person named Mandzo?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which room he was in and where you were when you saw him being taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This person Mandzo, if you're asking me about a person who was beaten up together with that salesperson, I am answering you in that connection. At that time, I was in the room next door. In the same hallway, there were two other rooms and there was a single entrance door so all these rooms and all of us were there together, room by room. And there was one door. So I was next door to where Mandzo was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which part of the building was this?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first building, downstairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned a person called Dzanko?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which room was he in?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same room where Mandzo was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he taken out at the same time when Mandzo was taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you the exact minutes and seconds. We saw them being taken out, they were beaten up, they were returned and I mentioned that Dr. Berberkic sewed up this man's face. So suffice it to say that that happened, and we have said enough about this salesperson. I know one thing. I mean I didn't know this salesperson very well and I didn't know Mandzo very well either. They lived a bit further away from me but I got to know them down there and they were taken away and there has been no trace of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that they were returned and then sewn up. When were they returned? Were they taken out together?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They went missing at the same time, and they have never been seen since. Now, let me tell you whether I can give you the exact second when they were taken away. Again, I say I'd have to be a computer. I'd have to have a video camera, I mean to record all of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sir, we've heard all of this. You must be doing this deliberately. We have told you so often not to repeat yourself and to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I asked you about Dzelilovic, Vahida, Mandzo, Dzanko. Did you have contact with their families when you got out of the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With Mandzo's mother. I worked with her at the presidency for refugees and I talked to her personally. I cannot tell you how I talked to her. I talked to her personally and it was in that place where I told you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which Mandzo?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one who was beaten up together with that salesperson. He was a male nurse by profession.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that Mandzo nicknamed Kelta?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I am talking -- I said straight away, if we are talking about Mandzo from that room, then he's a male nurse, whereas Kelta is free. Kelta got out, Kelta was released, Mandzo Kelta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you work with the mother of this Mandzo?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: She came to this office in Sarajevo. It has its presidency for displaced persons and refugees so all parents whose children were killed in the notorious camp are crying and weeping until the present day. So I would kindly ask the honourable judges to tell this gentleman not to pester me asking me questions like this. Because this woman is still screaming, not only crying, she is devastated. I told you about this office in Sarajevo where men and women still come in sobbing and crying because of all these young people who were killed. I don't know what to tell you anymore. All right. Well, ask me and I'll answer you, but that's where I talked to her. Right now she is in a foreign country. I don't know which country. She told me which country. But she came to this presidency where we have these offices of ours in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you work in this office for displaced persons?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did work there, sir, for two years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At what time, which two years are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I worked there for two years. There are documents to prove that and now I don't know what this means to you. I mean asking me at what time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Look sir --

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just stop for a moment, please. I've told you twice today already it's not for you to determine what is relevant and what is not. I assume that you've come here in an endeavour to assist the Tribunal by giving the evidence that you have. But the evidence that you give is of little value to us unless it has been tested to see whether it's true, and this is the means by which it is tested. Now, I know you don't like it and I wouldn't like to be under a cross-examination myself, but if you do wish to assist this Tribunal, I'm afraid you just have to answer these questions. The question which is asked of you is when did you work for that organisation. That is relevant to test the assertion that you have made that these persons have never been heard of again. We want to know when it was you were working there and when you would have had the opportunity to have heard of them again. Now, if you're not going to answer the question, just say so. It means, of course, that your evidence will carry little weight. But I suggest to you if you answer the question, it will save us all a great deal of time and it may well assist us in accepting your evidence.

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do apologise, Your Honours. I am going to answer the gentleman's question. (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you talk to the persons who came there as displaced persons? Did you talk about what had happened in Foca?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not that we only talked over there. These stories are heard throughout the world and I think that you know this full well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I asked you about four persons. You mentioned that you had had contact with a certain person called Mandzo?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the rest?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The rest? I might have had contact with them, but without knowing their names. But I knew this woman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday you mentioned Nurko Nisic, sir. Do you know which room he was taken out of?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nurko Nisic was taken out -- again I'm telling you that I was not interested in the numbers of rooms. He was taken out of the first Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. building. When Nurko Nisic was tortured, when he screamed, we all recognised his voice, because he got married very young, he was a well-developed man. They beat him so badly that perhaps his screams could have been heard to the centre of Foca, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you at that moment?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time I was in that room over there, in the isolated room, in another building. I heard it even from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this the isolation cell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I said that the four of us had a separate room. It was not an isolation cell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which building is this? The second one?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what time of the day it was?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was also in the early evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you mentioned Halim Konjo as well, sir. Do you know which room he was taken out of?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Halim Konjo was taken out -- at that time I was also transferred to these rooms where they were, so his room was L -- if you look at this L-shape, Halim Konjo was at this L-shape and our windows were like this. So he could establish contact with us, and not only him, but everybody who was in that room, through the windows. It was nearby, a metre or two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was the first or second building?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At what time was he taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also early in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you then?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the room, in the room. At that time I was in the room, because when I was in the room, in the room where they were, then I was kicked out of the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which room were you in? In which part of the building?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first part of the building, the ground floor, diagonally, right above the door that was the exit and entrance into and out of the camp. I was about -- I was very close to the door, so we could see everything: who was taken out, everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the room above the storage area?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Just a minute. Just a minute. It's not. It's not. This room was here. The building is like this, here, here, here. And then we could watch from here, see, from this other side. Does this mean anything to you? I mean, it just so happened that I know this, and that's pretty important to me. I could see this. We were in this kind of room. It's not the room above the storage area, but it's over here, if this means anything to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it in the other part of the building?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's in the same building, the same building, but the L-shaped thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in a room that is closer to the administration building of the KP Dom, the part that is closer to the administration building of the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, viewed from this first part, perhaps it's 10 or 15 metres away. Not much difference, is it? Ten or fifteen metres, sort of protruding out here, sort of L-shaped, so it's closer to the offices.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the usher for his assistance. Could you please show us this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at this floor plan, 6/1. There's building number 1 and there's building number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could the usher please keep the floor plan there if we still need it.

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's this building here. This is building number 1. Part of the building here --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, we can see where the building is. Just show us where you were in terms of this specific question. In which room were you when you saw Halim Konjo being taken out and not returning?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This building here, this other one. If I'm knowledgeable enough as far as this drawing is concerned, there were these rooms here, so we could talk, if I'm knowledgeable enough as far as this drawing is concerned. I mean, there was this room here. This room was above the storage area, and this other room was in this other building. Perhaps I made a mistake a few moments ago, and I do apologise to this Honourable Court if I did that. So this room is in this building, and these prisoners who were here, that's where Halim Konjo also was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, let me say that on 6/1, the witness has been showing building number 1, the right-hand part of building number 1, and he says Halim Konjo was taken out of there and he's showing -- Please, sir, let me finish. He is showing building number 2, the protruding part of the building, the part that protrudes towards the administrative building, and he says that his room was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think it's not quite clear - at least, it's not clear enough to me - precisely where it was the witness says he was when he saw this man being taken out. I think he means in the L-shaped part of building 2. I'm not sure. So if you would like to pursue that matter, it will be of assistance to us. Thank you, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you're talking about building number 2, that you were there in that building. On which floor?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ground floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in this part which is closer to the administration building?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This part was closer. I would kindly ask the Honourable Court -- I mean, I don't know. I'm not very knowledgeable as far as this drawing is concerned, because I'm not an expert in construction or in mechanics. So could the Honourable Court please provide a photograph of the camp for me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We've got the sketch. That might be the best idea. Mr. Smith will be proud of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excellent. So if I see this correctly, I'll say the same thing that I said as far as the drawing was concerned as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, sir. No, don't tell us what is what. Sir, don't.

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in this building that has windows here, on this side, and on the other side. So there were more rooms here, where there were prisoners, and there were also rooms here were there were prisoners, and I don't know what you're asking me really.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for the transcript, the witness is showing the part of the building marked "B" on this sketch. He said that he was on the ground floor and that his windows were facing the building which is marked "A" on this sketch.

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Would you agree with that, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff? It seems to be so.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm sorry Mr. Smith wasn't here to see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, please. You mentioned the Rikalo brothers. Do you know where they were taken out of, from which room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The brothers Rikalo? I met them only at the camp. They were taken out. At that time I was working in the kitchen. Now, I don't know exactly whether I had been transferred from the kitchen, because for a while --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, sir. Just tell me: Do you know which room they were taken out of?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first building. I don't know the exact room. The first building. Because had I known the layout, if I knew where each prisoner was, I would have been the warden, if I would have known every room, every prisoner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's fine. Thank you, sir. That's enough. Were all the brothers taken out at the same time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One by one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they all in the same room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat it once again: Had I been distributing people around all the rooms, then I would have memorised them all, and if not there, then I would have had it noted down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you when brothers Rikalo were taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Brothers Rikalo, when they were taken out, would you believe it that at the time when they were taken out -- I don't know. You tell me I'm not answering you specifically. I don't know myself where I was, but if that means anything to you, I was in the building of the camp. Now, to tell you within a metre or two ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And Nail Hodzic, when he was taken, where was it from?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first building too, and beaten and battered and then taken out and disappeared, killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him being taken?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've told you about every one of them, at what time of the day, at what time of the night I was in that compound, and I pointed out that I did not see all the prisoners, because hundreds and hundreds of them were taken out, but I did see him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you when you saw him? From where did you see him being taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in this room which I just pointed out on the drawing, when he was beaten and when he passed on his way to meals and when he was taken away. I saw it all. I told you, I was in this building which is L-shaped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at what time of the day was he taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Early evening/late afternoon again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned yesterday Mustafa Kuloglija. Where was he taken out from?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mustafa Kuloglija, also in the early days, he also came from those rooms which were near us, on this other side. And upstairs there were also floors and there were also rooms there. And on the upper floor, on this drawing here, building A and then in this upper part, the upper part was filled and the lower part was filled and we moved from one building to another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment, sir. You moved the pointer, and I will ask you: Are you saying that it was building A?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Building A, like "L."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you say that the topmost floors were filled up.

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time all the rooms were filled up. Those were the early days of bringing in, beating, killing; and then some left, others came in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you are talking about the topmost floor of the building?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The building was completely full. I don't know how many prisoners there were. I only know that we came for meals. There were columns and columns of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you also mentioned an individual called Krunoslav Marinovic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What room was he taken out of that time when he did not come back again?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Krunoslav Marinovic was in a lower room in building A. He came beaten up, and after a while was taken out, killed, and is missing. There's no trace of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, sir, whether Mustafa Kuloglija and Nurko Nisic were taken out together, that is, at the same time or roughly at the same time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that groups and groups, if they took one group today and another group the next day, so that I cannot answer concretely to you, the Honourable Court, whether they went out together, because it was groups that left, one after another. And we watched non-stop how they were going away. At that time the number of killings was the highest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell us sir, where were you when Kruno Marinovic was taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When Krunoslav Marinovic was taken out, those were the early days because I know -- I've already said that I saw him battered completely. So that in the beginning I was there. That is, I lived in this lower part until we were transferred over there. Those were early days. And then when these extremists from Serbia, Montenegro left, a few of them were left behind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke about Dzanko, Nurko Nisic, Halim Konjo, Kuloglija, Marinovic. Did you communicate with some members of their family?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I communicated with the family -- with Kuloglija's relatives. I communicated with Klinac's family. I communicated with a close relative of the Gagovic woman, that is Krunoslav's, and she's his sister's daughter. I communicated with her in Foca, when they took me out to take out flour sacks from the bakery. I've told you people that I had communicated with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after you left the KP Dom, you communicated with Krunoslav Marinovic's family?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. With Krunoslav Marinovic's family, I spoke personally with his -- what's he to him? His sister's daughter is married to him, as he was passing by the bakery. And I said how -- I talked to him in Foca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question is quite clear. Did you communicate with Marinovic's family after your release from the prison?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but I did speak to them before I was released, in a bakery which is about 100 metres away from the prison and I was unloading some sacks of flour and he was passing by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you mentioned a person called Hamid Bico. What room was he taken from?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Same thing. Hamid Bico was also taken from this first. Now, whether he lived on that floor or on the ground floor but this first building at any rate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you when you saw him being taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are all early days. I think that I was in the kitchen at the time. Can't really remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what time of the day was it when he was taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Late afternoon, early evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that means what time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was spring, and it was late spring then. It was already dark so it could have been 4.00 or 5.00, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned a person called Zulfo Veiz. What room was he taken from?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the first building again. I think I also watched him being taken away from the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At what time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Same, late afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned a person called Mate Ivancic. What room was he taken from?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mate Ivancic was taken out from room L, upper floor, on the side. I don't know which room exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, building numbering 1?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, building number 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you then?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I was in the kitchen on that occasion, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it the same day when Mate Ivancic and those others were taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said they took one group today, the next group the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. next day, so as to make us believe that nothing was happening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And brothers Cancusic, where were they taken from, which room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Brothers Cancusic were also taken out in the beginning and were killed and are missing. And I also communicated with their parents in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you which room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether the L one or this one here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But is it the first building or the second building?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you when you saw that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I was in the kitchen, not quite 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned Seval Soro. Which room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again the same, first building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you at that time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I was in the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At what time of the day was he taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it looked like he was being taken away earlier than those others. He was supposedly to take something. When we asked about, we were told, well, he has to take a vehicle somewhere, to take something somewhere, but he didn't take anything anywhere or --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned Fuad Mandzo, sir.

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the Mandzo salesman?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. It is a young man. I think he was a builder -- a mason or something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was he taken out from?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was also taken from these first, and he was also beaten. I don't know exactly when he was taken away. I cannot remember that, but they beat him and beat him. And the other Mandzo, they also beat him. And so they beat him and took him away but I can't remember when exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him being taken away?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Enes Uzunovic yesterday, sir?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which room he was taken from?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember the room exactly but at the time when he was taken away, they -- he asked, "Should I take something with me?" And they said, "No, nothing."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that? Were you in the same room with him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was nearby. I was quite near. So that we communicated. Or be that as it may, but I saw it immediately when they took him out, everything, his personal papers and his clothes, all stayed behind. He was taken out, disappeared, was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you hear that exchange? In the yard or in the building?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I heard, I was told that by those who were in the room with him. I could not hear that because it was in another room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you see had him being taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him be taken out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was -- where were you when he was taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember, but I saw his clothes later on and all his papers and everything. Everything just stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, you also mentioned a person called Alija Altoka. Where was he taken out from?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first building again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At about what time of the day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really remember, believe me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you when you saw him being taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I was in the kitchen again when he was taken out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, you also mentioned a person called Adil Granov?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was he taken out from?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Adil Granov was also in the first building, somewhere, and from that first building, he was taken out and disappeared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At what time of the day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was still daylight. There was more daylight then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recollect whether I was in the kitchen or -- in the kitchen, in the kitchen. I know I worked in the kitchen at that time, and we called him because he was a big expert. He was a mechanical engineer and we called him to help us, to help us repair the potato peeler. And after that, he disappeared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he with a group or alone?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was taken alone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned a person called Munib Veiz?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was he taken out from?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was taken out with this group, Soro, the taxi driver, what's his name, that was the group that he was taken out with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Same room, I cannot say whether from rooms L or what, but the first building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you at that time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I was in the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what --

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because those were early days. I don't know at what time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you saw from the kitchen how they took out this group?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when I say "kitchen," it is the whole kitchen, this whole kitchen area. That is, caldron from which you can see it all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at about what time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time of the day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember the time of the day. I cannot remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the weather that day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that spring was very cloudy. That spring wept, if that means anything to you. The saddest time in my life, both in terms of the weather and as far as I'm personally concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you mentioned a person called Kemal Tulek?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was he taken out from?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He spent in the isolation cell all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was he taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, believe me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him being taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of that because it went on non-stop. They beat him non-stop. And I cannot really answer 100 per cent, and I do not want to lie before the court or before you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned a person called Ramo Dzendusic. Where was he taken out from?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ramo Dzendusic, I said the people who had moved in Foca, and I don't remember their surname. If you're talking about a salesman from Tabaci, one salesman from Tabaci was so beaten that he hanged himself. He simply couldn't stand the pain any more and he hanged himself. If that's the salesman, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, you don't know who I'm referring to?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. I'm saying if that is the salesman, because I could not those names remember. If it is -- if Ramo is that salesman that he was beaten up and he hanged himself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if it is another Dzendusic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two with that surname. I think there was one Dzendusic who worked in the military department, in the military office, up in the police station. He was in charge of military matters. If that is the one you mean, he was taken out and killed. If you mean the salesman, he was beaten up and he hanged himself. Their names sound alike but I didn't know them before. I never met them before. Even that one that worked in the police station, I never really met him. I may have seen him twice in my life altogether.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you know both Dzendusics before the war?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I may have seen this one twice and the other one once or twice, I mean the salesman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And before the war, did you know their names?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't, believe me, nor did I want to know them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you learn their names?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the prison, in the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see one of them being taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the one who had worked in the police station was responsible for military matters, because he trembled like a reed in the camp, and he was taken out and is missing. And I also communicated with his family, and they are not in Bosnia at the moment. I believe they are in Germany, but they came to Sarajevo and we communicated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us which room was he taken from?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one that was in the military office, he was taken out from my room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which part of the building?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first part of the building, ground floor, because he was in my room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time of the day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was daylight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in the room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was in the room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it in the early days?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say how many months. No, not right in the beginning. Several months had passed by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Weren't you working in the kitchen at the time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you that I worked in the kitchen and was kicked out of the kitchen at the time when there were those people who were so exhausted so emaciated, they were falling down, and I -- and then I was thrown out of the kitchen and stopped working in the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this Dzendusic, was he taken all by himself or with a group?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was alone when he was taken away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned a person called Juso Dzamalija. Where he was he taken out from?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those surnames, Dzendusic, Dzamalija, I can't tell one from the other because I cannot give an exact answer. I don't know all those surnames. I know what they look like, but I cannot tell the surnames, one from the other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how then can you say -- how can you recognise faces?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when you give me those surnames, it is more difficult for me to say which surname is which without a photograph, but I know that those surnames were tortured and killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You're not waiting for the translation to finish, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does this thing that you just said mean, "I know that those surnames were taken out and killed"? Yesterday, you said that Juso Dzamalija was taken out and killed. Now you tell us that you cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Juso Dzamalija was the person where the witness did not know the name. It was the conclusion of the Prosecution that this must be Juso Dzamalija, because the witness said one of these Dzendusics hanged himself. This is actually the name that the witness did not mention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think we'd have to look it up. I don't remember. I remember there was a very hotly disputed assignation by the Prosecution of one of these incidents. But if that's so, I don't think you could ask him about the name in those circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, but my notes say differently. But I'm not challenging what my learned friend has said and I shall move on so as not to waste more time on that. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You wish to leave now, sir? Do you want a break now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We'll take an early break. We'll resume at 11.20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I still have to ask you about four persons you mentioned. You mentioned a person named Mesa Sofradzija. Do you know which room he was taken out of?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mesa Sofradzija, I know that person well. He was taken out. He was first in the rooms and then he was taken out of the isolation cell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At what time of day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but it was sort of dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you when they took him out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I was in the kitchen then, in front of the caldron, when dinner was over and everything, the cleaning of the caldron.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say "sort of dark." For how long did dinner go on?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dinner? I can't remember exactly. See, I don't remember these times of the day very well. Before there was actual nightfall, we would stay there. We would stay there to clean up after dinner was over and when it was really dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in the kitchen, or rather, did you hear beatings when Mesa Sofradzija was taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We heard moans when they were beating him in the isolation cell. When they were beating him in the isolation cell, that's when I heard it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that same day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not on that day; on several occasions. I think he was beaten up several times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when he was taken out, you didn't hear anything?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear beatings then. He was just taken out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You said -- you mentioned a person named Rasim Kajgana. Where was he taken from?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was taken out -- we had already been transferred to the upper rooms. He was taken out of those rooms upstairs, the upper floors. I don't know exactly. I think building A, the top floor, so I know we were in that room too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Building A, top floor; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not 100 per cent sure, but he was a bit up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you when he was taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I was in the room then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The room where he had been.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were in the same room with him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I was, because I know when he was taken out -- when he was taken out to chop firewood, I was also taken out to chop firewood in the compound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you: When he was taken out, he was taken out of your room and you were in the room and you saw him taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not return. He never returned. I thought it was some kind of exchange. I saw his family in Sarajevo as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time you were in building A, on the top floor?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, something like that. Whether it was the last floor or not -- well, at any rate, I was in that building, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear beatings when he was taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't. I can't remember that I heard screams or something like that. I thought -- well, he had Mojevic. He asked him to release him, so I thought that perhaps he had arranged something through someone. He was Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. taken out and killed. I'm not sure, but I didn't hear him being tortured. At any rate, his entire family, everybody who is abroad, like his wife, they all came to Sarajevo, and talk, and there has been no trace of him since.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, was he taken out on his own?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on his own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember which time of the year it was when he was taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall that date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't ask you about the date, sir. I asked you about the time of year.

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, believe me, I can't even say what time of year it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned a person named Avdo Mehmedspahic. Where was he taken out from?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was taken out of the isolation cell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time of day?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime in the early evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you? Where did you see him being taken out?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I was in front of the kitchen caldron then or inside. I can't remember. At any rate, he was tortured, battered and taken away. I also talked to his family in Sarajevo. He was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he was taken out, did you hear the sounds of beatings?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I most often heard these sounds from the isolation cell, because they were one opposite the other. There was a short distance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that he was the person who was being beaten in the isolation cell?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted). So I knew him well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he was taken out, did you hear sounds of beatings?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned the Hadzimesic brothers?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were they taken out of?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Hadzimesic brothers, one was in one room and the other one was in the room opposite that one. I mean -- when I say "opposite," well, I don't know whether you know this expression, one was upstairs and the other one, I'm not 100 per cent sure, but at any rate it is in building

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was in the L-shaped part or whatever. But at any rate, I know when I was in this room here, I would see them go out. At that time, I had been thrown out of the kitchen so we saw them non-stop. They were going to have lunch so they could not pass by without passing by us, I mean by our windows.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they taken out together?

utterances.speaker: FWS-73 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. One by one, because this one was separated. I mean, if one was taken out one day, then the other one will be taken a few days later.
